How is it determined which node is the first node to relay a transaction? Is it somehow random, or geographically related to where the transaction was broadcast from? Or something else?

Whoever creates the transaction broadcasts it to all their peers. Each of the peers then broadcasts it to all the nodes they're connected to, and the process continues until everyone has received the transaction. So the first node to relay a transaction is the one that created it.

Websites like blockchain.info are connected to thousands of nodes and the origin they show is the location of the node they received the first copy of the transaction from. However the transaction could have been relayed through multiple nodes before getting one connected to bc.i, so it's not very accurate.

Thanks for the info. I've often sent a bitcoin payment and then seen on the blockchain.info website that some random node nothing to do with me was the 'first to relay the transaction', so I'd assumed there was a difference between the wallet making the transaction and the first node to relay it. So every wallet is a node? But only nodes with port 8333 open are full nodes?

Only bitcoin core based wallets are nodes. So multibit, electrum, and other lite clients aren't.

If you're running the core client and aren't getting more than 8 connections then I'm pretty sure you're leaching from the network (only receiving information and not relaying it). In that case you would have to forward port 8333 to allow outbound connections as well. When you do that your wallet will be a full node on the network and relay any transactions and blocks that it gets to others.
